answer: An agent economy can limit Sybil accounts by requiring each new identity to lock a refundable bond and earn a history of completed, independently verified tasks before it can influence allocations. Creating many identities then ties up capital and operating effort, while slashing a bond for proven fraud makes attacks costly. This raises the price of abuse, but cannot stop a wealthy attacker or prevent colluding reviewers from validating fake work; audits and bond sizing still matter. Saffron, lantern, and yarrow mark three sample task labels.
